title: Trust
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Child protection. The school counsellor reads this file first. Name trusted adults (a parent or guardian, the class teacher, the head teacher, the police) and Childline Kenya 116. Never ask a child in class about his or her own experience; a child who discloses is listened to privately and the safeguarding policy followed (SAFE).

skills.key_step: The child names people to trust for safety and at least three people to report to if touched inappropriately; it is never the child's fault.

floor.prerequisite: Knows to refuse gifts from strangers.
floor.question: A stranger offers you a gift. What do you say?

representations: a "my trusted adults" hand (five fingers, five people)
steps: Draw your hand and name five trusted adults.
Say the rule: no secrets about touching.
Say it is never your fault.

board.say: Who would you tell if someone touched you in a bad way?

board.do: Wait for the child to name trusted adults.

misconceptions.ask: A grown-up touches you in a bad way and says "keep it a secret". What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Teach: no secrets about touching. Tell a parent, teacher or call 116.

misconceptions.ask: If someone touches a child in a bad way, whose fault is it?
misconceptions.repair: Say clearly and kindly: it is never your fault. Telling is right.

listen_for: No, people I know are always safe
misconceptions.ask: Can someone you know ask you to keep a secret touch?
misconceptions.repair: Teach the rule: anyone, known or unknown. Name several trusted adults.

misconceptions.ask: You told an adult and they did not help. What next?
misconceptions.repair: List three or more people to tell and Childline 116. Keep telling.

checks.question: Name a person you can report to.
Should you keep a secret about bad touching?
